thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Canary anomaly detected for model redwood/enginetest-v1.3.2 — spike in 5xx and tail latency at 03:07 UTC. Auto-canary rollout paused by policy. Metrics: 5xx rate 4.2% (baseline 0.1%), p95 latency 2.3s -> 6.8s.
Tom Hsu: Acked. I'm on call. /pd ack #incidents
Maya Chen: I'm on ML side — saw weird diffs when comparing canary vs prod samples. Short completions are being truncated frequently, some responses end mid-token.
Ashwin Rao: Looking at logs now. Sharing a log excerpt from canary host (redwood-canary-gpu-12):
```
[2026-03-15T03:06:49Z] request_id=abc123 model=redwood/enginetest-v1.3.2 recv=32ms decode=12ms infer=6200ms error=RuntimeError: kv_cache mismatch
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/infer.py", line 482, in forward
    kv = self.kv_cache.get(key)
KeyError: 'kv-0-128'
```
Ashwin Rao: Also see repeated "decode failed: unexpected token len" in decoder logs.
Dena Patel: Product-ops — quick customer impact: ~4% of hosted requests are failing during the canary window. Two customers on Dedicated might be affected (acct: acme-corp, acct: nova-ai) — both flagged high-priority.
Priya Singh: Are Dedicated clusters on v1.3.2 as well or pinned to earlier? I can check.
ML Platform Bot: Query results: dedicated_assignments where model_version = 'v1.3.2' -> acme-corp-1 (false), nova-ai-3 (true). Nova-ai has a pinned instance on v1.3.2.
Tom Hsu: Hypotheses: 1) Runtime KV cache format changed between v1.3.1 -> v1.3.2 (quantization or cache key shape mismatch). 2) Tokenizer update caused unexpected token lengths. 3) New fused kernel on canary hardware exposes a bug (kernel/driver mismatch).
Maya Chen: I diffed the model packaging. v1.3.2 introduced an optional int4 quant path and bumped tokenizer crate to 0.12. Small change but could affect decode flows.
Ashwin Rao: Running a targeted canary diff between sample traces (prod v1.3.1 vs canary v1.3.2). Put results in pastebin: https://paste.redwood.internal/abcd1234 (contains side-by-side token stream). Key observation: canary emits extra sentinel token bytes before finalization -> decoder loops then hits kv cache KeyError.
Tom Hsu: Immediate mitigation options:
- Roll forward fix (fast patch) — risky to build and deploy quick.
- Rollback canary -> pin to v1.3.1 and resume canary with new hardware/flags.
- Temporary routing: divert traffic from canary to stable pool and unpause rollout after validation.
What do we want to do now? We should avoid touching Dedicated pinned instances until we confirm.
Priya Singh: I'll hold on interactions with Nova-AI until we confirm. If rollback required, coordinate with SEs.
Dena Patel: Customer comms draft in #customer-ops: "We observed increased errors for a subset of requests during routine canary rollout. We are investigating; we may rollback the canary to restore service. We'll update within 1h." (:+1:)
Ashwin Rao: I'm running a quick query to check who has model pinned. SQL I used:
```
-- find pinned deployments
SELECT customer, cluster, pinned_version
FROM model_deployments
WHERE model_name = 'enginetest' AND pinned_version IS NOT NULL;
```
ML Platform Bot: Query result (abridged): ["nova-ai","nova-cluster-3","v1.3.2"]
Tom Hsu: Given dedicated pinned customer, we won't force-push to their cluster. Action plan for now:
1) Pause any further canary promotions. (done — rollout controller: paused)
2) Divert incoming canary traffic to stable pool. (routing rule updated)
3) Pin traffic away from canary hosts — run immediate rollback for canary group.
4) Start full log collection (all inference nodes, decoders, tokenizer traces) and timeline building.
Ashwin Rao: Executed: `redwoodctl rollout hold --model=enginetest --group=canary` -> ok
Tom Hsu: Routing change done: canary -> stable. /deploy status shows stable serving at previous capacity.
Maya Chen: I'm pushing a patch to disable int4 quant path and re-run canary in isolated env. That should remove the new code path quickly.
Priya Singh: SE note: Nova-AI pinned cluster unaffected by routing change, but we're preparing a safe rollback plan that won't alter pinned clusters.
Dena Patel: Customer impact numbers updated: failures peaked at 5.1% at 03:08 UTC, dropped to 0.2% after diversion. Logged incident ticket: INC-2026-1158 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-1158). I've added acme-corp and nova-ai as impacted customers.
Ashwin Rao: Sharing a compact timeline (building as we go):
- 03:00 UTC: Canary rollout v1.3.2 begins (10% traffic)
- 03:05 UTC: p95 latency increases, first 5xx spike
- 03:06 UTC: KV cache KeyError appears in canary hosts
- 03:07 UTC: Incident Bot pages SRE (this thread root)
- 03:10 UTC: Rollout controller auto-paused
- 03:12 UTC: Routing diverted canary traffic to stable
- 03:20 UTC: Failures back down to baseline for hosted traffic
- 03:28 UTC: DS/ML reproduce decode loop locally
Tom Hsu: We should still collect heap/core dumps from one failing canary node for postmortem. Ashwin, can you request node snapshot and attach to the ticket?
Ashwin Rao: On it. `gcloud compute instances snapshot redwood-canary-gpu-12 --zone=us-west1-b` -> snapshot job started. I'll upload logs to INC-2026-1158.
Maya Chen: Quick repro note: running local infer with v1.3.2 model + test prompt triggers "decoder unexpected token" ~1/20 runs on CPU emulation; reproduces reliably using the quantized path flag `--use-quant=int4`.
Tom Hsu: Decision: rollback canary group to v1.3.1 and pin canary group to v1.3.1 until a patch passes regression tests. Do NOT touch Dedicated pinned clusters.
Priya Singh: I'll notify SEs for Nova-AI and let them know we are not changing their pinned cluster. They'll watch.
Dena Patel: Comms: "We rolled back the canary to v1.3.1 and diverted canary traffic to stable pools. Dedicated/pinned customer clusters are unchanged. Investigation in progress. Next update in 30m or on-change." (sent to affected customers)
Tom Hsu: Rollback command executed: `redwoodctl rollout rollback --model=enginetest --group=canary --to-version=v1.3.1` -> success.
ML Platform Bot: Rollback completed. Canary group now serving v1.3.1. Canary failure rate normal.
Ashwin Rao: Uploaded logs + snapshot to INC-2026-1158, added diff artifacts and token stream paste.
Maya Chen: Plan for post-incident RCA:
- Root cause hypothesis: int4 quant path introduced a KV cache key-shape regression under certain batch shapes -> decoder error.
- Action items: revert int4 path in next patch (short-term), add unit/regression tests for tokenizer/kv cache boundary shapes, add canary test harness that exercises quant code on small sequences.
- Owner: Maya (patch), Ashwin (logs+repro), Tom (oncall/RCA doc)
Tom Hsu: Scheduling a 1-hour RCA sync at 04:30 UTC. Invite: #incidents, ml-platform, eng-runtime, product-ops. Please add notes to INC ticket.
Dena Patel: I'll update postmortem template and include customer timeline and comms artifacts.
Priya Singh: After-action: check all release automation for accidental off-by-one in cache key serialization (I have a quick grep/PR going).
Tom Hsu: Thanks everyone. Closing this live thread now as mitigation complete. We'll keep the ticket open for RCA artifacts. :white_check_mark:
Incident Bot: Incident resolved status changed to: mitigated (root-cause-investigation ongoing)"
